updated and regression tests added.

Closes #279

item.title: feat(nature-paper2word): add Markdown → Word skill (documentation only)
item.description:
feat(nature-paper2word): add Markdown → Word skill (documentation only)

Adds a documentation-only skill that compiles a Markdown manuscript into a
journal- or school-compliant Word file. The engine is the PyPI package
md-to-word-docx; the skill carries the router only.

- SKILL.md: scenario, manuscript contract, requirements file, export, gates
- README.md / README_EN.md: mirrored entry pages, eight sections each
- manifest.yaml, agents/openai.yaml: manifest and interface metadata
- Registers the skill in the README index and the project site, and adds its
  path to the skill-tooling workflow
item.label: commit

item.title: docs(nature-figure): panel gaps, tick steps, aspect and labelling con…
item.description:
docs(nature-figure): panel gaps, tick steps, aspect and labelling conventions

Let the content set a figure's height within an author's aspect rule (a row
of bar charts reads better wider than 4:3), keep gaps between panels to what
their labels need, set tick values in the data's own steps rather than the
locator's after a resize, and verify the journal's panel-labelling
convention before changing it. In the schematic rules, ask for a sketch
when a layout described in words can be read two ways.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: docs(nature-figure): measure printed size; connector and label rules
item.description:
docs(nature-figure): measure printed size; connector and label rules

Add to the QA contract a section on the size figure text prints at in the
compiled manuscript: read the caption size from the document class, set
figure text a little below it, and account for the three things that change
the printed size without changing the source (rescaling a tightly cropped
figure to the text width, TeX versus PDF points, x-height differences
between faces). Verify by measuring x-heights on the rendered page. Add a
section on multi-line labels, whose Matplotlib leading varies with the
alignment, and rules on panel titles, legend placement and palettes.

In the schematic style rules, let unconnected lines cross plainly (a gap
reads as a break), attach connectors at the middle, a third or a quarter of
a side, keep them straight with at most one bend and off box edges, space
repeated cards equally, bold only top-level names, and ask when layout
constraints conflict.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: docs(nature-figure): agent diagrams, implementation check and text rules
item.description:
docs(nature-figure): agent diagrams, implementation check and text rules

Add an "Agent and tool diagrams" section to the vector schematic style
rules: draw an LLM agent as its iterating loop with the tools as callees,
calls leaving the tool-call station and results returning to the
observation station, and retrieval as one more tool call.

Ask the brief to be checked against the implementation (code,
configuration, methods), render and inspect the edited region after every
revision, and add rules on one dark ink, short box text, even justified
spacing, broken crossings, and shared widths for boxes of one role. In
the default stance, do not print a value on every mark.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-academic-search): make --retry 0 still try once in format-…
item.description:
fix(nature-academic-search): make --retry 0 still try once in format-converter

efetch_medline, download_crossref and download_arxiv looped over range(retries),
so --retry 0 skipped the loop entirely: download_crossref then hit
UnboundLocalError on `data`, and the other two returned nothing. Use
max(1, retries) attempts. Adds tests for a successful and a failing download.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-figure): report OpenRouter timeouts and image download fai…
item.description:
fix(nature-figure): report OpenRouter timeouts and image download failures cleanly

request_images only caught HTTPError and URLError, so a socket timeout while
waiting for headers or reading the body escaped as a raw TimeoutError traceback
after the request had already been sent (and billed). The second urlopen that
fetches item["url"] had no handler at all. Catch OSError/TimeoutError for both
and exit with a clear message. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-response): resolve \input of a dotted filename like sec1.f…
item.description:
fix(nature-response): resolve \input of a dotted filename like sec1.final

check_package_consistency appended ".tex" only when the target had no suffix, so
\input{sec1.final} (a file named sec1.final.tex) looked for "sec1.final", failed
is_file(), and the include was left unexpanded; the checker then silently skipped
that section's text. Follow LaTeX: try name.tex first, then the literal name.
Adds tests, including explicit .tex and extensionless existing files.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix: match a top-level --output path in the star-history README cache…
item.description:
fix: match a top-level --output path in the star-history README cache-buster

For `--output star-history.svg` PurePosixPath(...).parent is ".", so the pattern
required a literal "./" prefix and matched nothing: the SVG was written, then
update_readme_cache_buster raised RuntimeError and left the README stale.
Omit the directory prefix for a top-level file and anchor the match so it does
not rewrite a longer filename such as other-star-history.svg. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix: leave the star-history chart unchanged when stargazer counts dis…
item.description:
fix: leave the star-history chart unchanged when stargazer counts disagree

fetch_stargazers raised StarHistoryUnavailable ("leaving the existing chart
unchanged") when GitHub's reported count and the returned timestamps differ by
more than 100, but main only caught that exception around build_daily_points, so
the job crashed with a traceback and exit 1 instead of warning and returning 0.
Catch it around the fetch too. A missing token is a configuration error, so it
now raises a StarHistoryAuthRequired subclass that still fails the job. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-academic-search): skip arXiv error entries instead of retu…
item.description:
fix(nature-academic-search): skip arXiv error entries instead of returning a paper

arXiv reports a bad request as an <entry> with id http://arxiv.org/api/errors#...
and title "Error". The id regex matched the trailing NNNN.NNNNN, so
get_by_id("2401.99999") returned {"title": "Error", ...} instead of raising
"Paper not found". Skip entries whose id is an /api/errors URL. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-academic-search): ignore Scopus "Result set was empty" ent…
item.description:
fix(nature-academic-search): ignore Scopus "Result set was empty" entries

Scopus answers an empty search with entry: [{"error": "Result set was empty"}].
_search_entries passed that dict through, so search("TITLE(xyz)") returned
total 0 plus one phantom result with every field null. Drop entries carrying an
"error" key (ScienceDirect already filtered its equivalent). Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-downloader): require an open licence before calling an art…
item.description:
fix(nature-downloader): require an open licence before calling an article OA

confirmedOa and the publisher_oa candidate treated any Crossref licence URL as
proof of open access, but paywalled articles routinely carry publisher TDM or
user licences (for example elsevier.com/tdm/userlicense/1.0), so a subscription
article was reported as "confirmed_oa" even when Unpaywall said it was closed.
Only a Creative Commons licence (URL or cc-by style token) now counts. Adds
tests for the TDM case and the CC URL case.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-downloader): do not overwrite a saved paper that has the s…
item.description:
fix(nature-downloader): do not overwrite a saved paper that has the same title

saveFullTextResponse named the file from the title (or DOI, or the literal
"article" fallback) and renameSync replaced any existing file, so a second paper
with the same title ("Editorial"), or any two direct --pdf-url downloads
without a title, silently destroyed the first and left the manifest sha256 for
it pointing at the wrong bytes. Add -2, -3, ... when the existing file has
different content, and reuse the file when the bytes are identical. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

ratio and recording the px_per_inch actually used. Adds tests.

with the same title ("Editorial"), or any two direct --pdf-url downloads
without a title, silently destroyed the first and left the manifest sha256 for
it pointing at the wrong bytes. Add -2, -3, ... when the existing file has
different content, and reuse the file when the bytes are identical. Adds tests.

item.title: fix(nature-response): resolve \input of a dotted filename like sec1.f…
item.description:
fix(nature-response): resolve \input of a dotted filename like sec1.final

check_package_consistency appended ".tex" only when the target had no suffix, so
\input{sec1.final} (a file named sec1.final.tex) looked for "sec1.final", failed
is_file(), and the include was left unexpanded; the checker then silently skipped
that section's text. Follow LaTeX: try name.tex first, then the literal name.
Adds tests, including explicit .tex and extensionless existing files.

item.title: fix: match a top-level --output path in the star-history README cache…
item.description:
fix: match a top-level --output path in the star-history README cache-buster

For `--output star-history.svg` PurePosixPath(...).parent is ".", so the pattern
required a literal "./" prefix and matched nothing: the SVG was written, then
update_readme_cache_buster raised RuntimeError and left the README stale.
Omit the directory prefix for a top-level file and anchor the match so it does
not rewrite a longer filename such as other-star-history.svg. Adds tests.

item.title: fix: leave the star-history chart unchanged when stargazer counts dis…
item.description:
fix: leave the star-history chart unchanged when stargazer counts disagree

fetch_stargazers raised StarHistoryUnavailable ("leaving the existing chart
unchanged") when GitHub's reported count and the returned timestamps differ by
more than 100, but main only caught that exception around build_daily_points, so
the job crashed with a traceback and exit 1 instead of warning and returning 0.

item.description:

arXiv reports a bad request as an <entry> with id http://arxiv.org/api/errors#...
and title "Error". The id regex matched the trailing NNNN.NNNNN, so
get_by_id("2401.99999") returned {"title": "Error", ...} instead of raising

total 0 plus one phantom result with every field null. Drop entries carrying an

item.title: fix(nature-downloader): require an open licence before calling an art…
item.description:
fix(nature-downloader): require an open licence before calling an article OA

confirmedOa and the publisher_oa candidate treated any Crossref licence URL as
proof of open access, but paywalled articles routinely carry publisher TDM or
user licences (for example elsevier.com/tdm/userlicense/1.0), so a subscription
article was reported as "confirmed_oa" even when Unpaywall said it was closed.
Only a Creative Commons licence (URL or cc-by style token) now counts. Adds
tests for the TDM case and the CC URL case.

item.title: fix(nature-downloader): do not overwrite a saved paper that has the s…
item.description:
fix(nature-downloader): do not overwrite a saved paper that has the same title

saveFullTextResponse named the file from the title (or DOI, or the literal
"article" fallback) and renameSync replaced any existing file, so a second paper
with the same title ("Editorial"), or any two direct --pdf-url downloads
without a title, silently destroyed the first and left the manifest sha256 for
it pointing at the wrong bytes. Add -2, -3, ... when the existing file has
different content, and reuse the file when the bytes are identical. Adds tests.

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): keep source-size slides within PowerPoint's 56…
item.description:
fix(nature-image2ppt): keep source-size slides within PowerPoint's 56 in limit

source_size_slide divided pixels by a fixed 96, so a 6000x3000 image produced a
62.5 in wide <p:sldSz> that PowerPoint rejects (its maximum is 56 in per side).
Use a coarser px/inch when either side would exceed 56 in, keeping the aspect
ratio and recording the px_per_inch actually used. Adds tests.

item.description:
fix(nature-image2ppt): resolve package-absolute OPC relationship targets

posixpath.join("ppt", "/ppt/slides/slide1.xml") returns the absolute path
unchanged, so a relationship Target written as "/ppt/..." (valid OPC) no longer
matched any zip member: the slide read raised KeyError (not caught as the
ValueError normalize_inputs expects) and image parts were reported missing even
though they were present. Add join_part() that treats a leading "/" as the
package root and use it for resolve_target and both slide-part joins. Adds
tests.

black), so a PNG with a transparent background became a black slide

first. Adds tests, including partial alpha and opaque pixels unchanged.

fetch_stargazers raised StarHistoryUnavailable ("leaving the existing chart
unchanged") when GitHub's reported count and the returned timestamps differ by
more than 100, but main only caught that exception around build_daily_points, so
the job crashed with a traceback and exit 1 instead of warning and returning 0.
Catch it around the fetch too. A missing token is a configuration error, so it
now raises a StarHistoryAuthRequired subclass that still fails the job. Adds tests.

item.title: fix(nature-academic-search): skip arXiv error entries instead of retu…
item.description:

arXiv reports a bad request as an <entry> with id http://arxiv.org/api/errors#...
and title "Error". The id regex matched the trailing NNNN.NNNNN, so
get_by_id("2401.99999") returned {"title": "Error", ...} instead of raising
"Paper not found". Skip entries whose id is an /api/errors URL. Adds tests.

item.title: fix(nature-downloader): do not overwrite a saved paper that has the s…

saveFullTextResponse named the file from the title (or DOI, or the literal

with the same title ("Editorial"), or any two direct --pdf-url downloads
without a title, silently destroyed the first and left the manifest sha256 for
it pointing at the wrong bytes. Add -2, -3, ... when the existing file has
different content, and reuse the file when the bytes are identical. Adds tests.

posixpath.join("ppt", "/ppt/slides/slide1.xml") returns the absolute path
unchanged, so a relationship Target written as "/ppt/..." (valid OPC) no longer
matched any zip member: the slide read raised KeyError (not caught as the
ValueError normalize_inputs expects) and image parts were reported missing even
though they were present. Add join_part() that treats a leading "/" as the
package root and use it for resolve_target and both slide-part joins. Adds
tests.

black), so a PNG with a transparent background became a black slide
background. Composite RGBA/LA/palette-with-transparency images onto white
first. Adds tests, including partial alpha and opaque pixels unchanged.

is_file(), and the include was left unexpanded; the checker then silently skipped
that section's text. Follow LaTeX: try name.tex first, then the literal name.

item.description:
fix(nature-image2ppt): never delete an existing --keep-workdir directory

_maybe_keep_workdir called shutil.rmtree on the target whenever it existed, so
`formula render-latex --keep-workdir assets` (accepted because assets/ is inside
the page directory) deleted every image in the page's assets folder before
copying the TeX debug files in. Refuse an existing non-empty target that was not
written by this command (marker file), check it before rendering so it cannot
mask a LaTeX error, and still replace its own previous copy. Adds tests.

item.title: fix(nature-academic-search): make --retry 0 still try once in format-…
item.description:

efetch_medline, download_crossref and download_arxiv looped over range(retries),
so --retry 0 skipped the loop entirely: download_crossref then hit
UnboundLocalError on `data`, and the other two returned nothing. Use
max(1, retries) attempts. Adds tests for a successful and a failing download.

item.title: fix(nature-figure): report OpenRouter timeouts and image download fai…
item.description:
fix(nature-figure): report OpenRouter timeouts and image download failures cleanly

request_images only caught HTTPError and URLError, so a socket timeout while
waiting for headers or reading the body escaped as a raw TimeoutError traceback
after the request had already been sent (and billed). The second urlopen that
fetches item["url"] had no handler at all. Catch OSError/TimeoutError for both
and exit with a clear message. Adds tests.

item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-response): resolve \input of a dotted filename like sec1.f…
item.description:
fix(nature-response): resolve \input of a dotted filename like sec1.final

check_package_consistency appended ".tex" only when the target had no suffix, so
\input{sec1.final} (a file named sec1.final.tex) looked for "sec1.final", failed
is_file(), and the include was left unexpanded; the checker then silently skipped
that section's text. Follow LaTeX: try name.tex first, then the literal name.
Adds tests, including explicit .tex and extensionless existing files.

item.title: fix: match a top-level --output path in the star-history README cache…
item.description:
fix: match a top-level --output path in the star-history README cache-buster

For `--output star-history.svg` PurePosixPath(...).parent is ".", so the pattern
required a literal "./" prefix and matched nothing: the SVG was written, then
update_readme_cache_buster raised RuntimeError and left the README stale.
Omit the directory prefix for a top-level file and anchor the match so it does
not rewrite a longer filename such as other-star-history.svg. Adds tests.

item.title: fix: leave the star-history chart unchanged when stargazer counts dis…
item.description:
fix: leave the star-history chart unchanged when stargazer counts disagree

fetch_stargazers raised StarHistoryUnavailable ("leaving the existing chart
unchanged") when GitHub's reported count and the returned timestamps differ by
more than 100, but main only caught that exception around build_daily_points, so
the job crashed with a traceback and exit 1 instead of warning and returning 0.
Catch it around the fetch too. A missing token is a configuration error, so it
now raises a StarHistoryAuthRequired subclass that still fails the job. Adds tests.

get_by_id("2401.99999") returned {"title": "Error", ...} instead of raising

total 0 plus one phantom result with every field null. Drop entries carrying an
"error" key (ScienceDirect already filtered its equivalent). Adds tests.

item.description:
fix(nature-downloader): require an open licence before calling an article OA

confirmedOa and the publisher_oa candidate treated any Crossref licence URL as
proof of open access, but paywalled articles routinely carry publisher TDM or
user licences (for example elsevier.com/tdm/userlicense/1.0), so a subscription
article was reported as "confirmed_oa" even when Unpaywall said it was closed.

tests for the TDM case and the CC URL case.

item.title: fix(nature-downloader): do not overwrite a saved paper that has the s…
item.description:
fix(nature-downloader): do not overwrite a saved paper that has the same title

saveFullTextResponse named the file from the title (or DOI, or the literal
"article" fallback) and renameSync replaced any existing file, so a second paper
with the same title ("Editorial"), or any two direct --pdf-url downloads
without a title, silently destroyed the first and left the manifest sha256 for
it pointing at the wrong bytes. Add -2, -3, ... when the existing file has
different content, and reuse the file when the bytes are identical. Adds tests.

item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): keep source-size slides within PowerPoint's 56…
item.description:
fix(nature-image2ppt): keep source-size slides within PowerPoint's 56 in limit

source_size_slide divided pixels by a fixed 96, so a 6000x3000 image produced a
62.5 in wide <p:sldSz> that PowerPoint rejects (its maximum is 56 in per side).
Use a coarser px/inch when either side would exceed 56 in, keeping the aspect
ratio and recording the px_per_inch actually used. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): resolve package-absolute OPC relationship targets
item.description:
fix(nature-image2ppt): resolve package-absolute OPC relationship targets

posixpath.join("ppt", "/ppt/slides/slide1.xml") returns the absolute path
unchanged, so a relationship Target written as "/ppt/..." (valid OPC) no longer
matched any zip member: the slide read raised KeyError (not caught as the
ValueError normalize_inputs expects) and image parts were reported missing even
though they were present. Add join_part() that treats a leading "/" as the
package root and use it for resolve_target and both slide-part joins. Adds
tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): flatten transparent images onto white, not black
item.description:
fix(nature-image2ppt): flatten transparent images onto white, not black

save_image_page and extract_image_based_pptx_pages used convert("RGB"), which
drops alpha and exposes the colour stored under transparent pixels (normally
black), so a PNG with a transparent background became a black slide
background. Composite RGBA/LA/palette-with-transparency images onto white
first. Adds tests, including partial alpha and opaque pixels unchanged.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): never delete an existing --keep-workdir directory
item.description:
fix(nature-image2ppt): never delete an existing --keep-workdir directory

_maybe_keep_workdir called shutil.rmtree on the target whenever it existed, so
`formula render-latex --keep-workdir assets` (accepted because assets/ is inside
the page directory) deleted every image in the page's assets folder before
copying the TeX debug files in. Refuse an existing non-empty target that was not
written by this command (marker file), check it before rendering so it cannot
mask a LaTeX error, and still replace its own previous copy. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma

item.title: fix(nature-downloader): do not overwrite a saved paper that has the s…
item.description:
fix(nature-downloader): do not overwrite a saved paper that has the same title

saveFullTextResponse named the file from the title (or DOI, or the literal
"article" fallback) and renameSync replaced any existing file, so a second paper
with the same title ("Editorial"), or any two direct --pdf-url downloads
without a title, silently destroyed the first and left the manifest sha256 for
it pointing at the wrong bytes. Add -2, -3, ... when the existing file has
different content, and reuse the file when the bytes are identical. Adds tests.

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): keep source-size slides within PowerPoint's 56…
item.description:
fix(nature-image2ppt): keep source-size slides within PowerPoint's 56 in limit

source_size_slide divided pixels by a fixed 96, so a 6000x3000 image produced a
62.5 in wide <p:sldSz> that PowerPoint rejects (its maximum is 56 in per side).
Use a coarser px/inch when either side would exceed 56 in, keeping the aspect
ratio and recording the px_per_inch actually used. Adds tests.

item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): resolve package-absolute OPC relationship targets
item.description:
fix(nature-image2ppt): resolve package-absolute OPC relationship targets

posixpath.join("ppt", "/ppt/slides/slide1.xml") returns the absolute path
unchanged, so a relationship Target written as "/ppt/..." (valid OPC) no longer
matched any zip member: the slide read raised KeyError (not caught as the
ValueError normalize_inputs expects) and image parts were reported missing even
though they were present. Add join_part() that treats a leading "/" as the
package root and use it for resolve_target and both slide-part joins. Adds
tests.

item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): flatten transparent images onto white, not black
item.description:
fix(nature-image2ppt): flatten transparent images onto white, not black

save_image_page and extract_image_based_pptx_pages used convert("RGB"), which
drops alpha and exposes the colour stored under transparent pixels (normally
black), so a PNG with a transparent background became a black slide
background. Composite RGBA/LA/palette-with-transparency images onto white
first. Adds tests, including partial alpha and opaque pixels unchanged.

item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): never delete an existing --keep-workdir directory
item.description:
fix(nature-image2ppt): never delete an existing --keep-workdir directory

_maybe_keep_workdir called shutil.rmtree on the target whenever it existed, so
`formula render-latex --keep-workdir assets` (accepted because assets/ is inside
the page directory) deleted every image in the page's assets folder before
copying the TeX debug files in. Refuse an existing non-empty target that was not
written by this command (marker file), check it before rendering so it cannot
mask a LaTeX error, and still replace its own previous copy. Adds tests.

fix(nature-response): resolve \input of a dotted filename like sec1.final

item.title: fix: match a top-level --output path in the star-history README cache…
item.description:
fix: match a top-level --output path in the star-history README cache-buster

For `--output star-history.svg` PurePosixPath(...).parent is ".", so the pattern
required a literal "./" prefix and matched nothing: the SVG was written, then
update_readme_cache_buster raised RuntimeError and left the README stale.
Omit the directory prefix for a top-level file and anchor the match so it does
not rewrite a longer filename such as other-star-history.svg. Adds tests.

item.title: fix: leave the star-history chart unchanged when stargazer counts dis…
item.description:
fix: leave the star-history chart unchanged when stargazer counts disagree

fetch_stargazers raised StarHistoryUnavailable ("leaving the existing chart
unchanged") when GitHub's reported count and the returned timestamps differ by
more than 100, but main only caught that exception around build_daily_points, so
the job crashed with a traceback and exit 1 instead of warning and returning 0.
Catch it around the fetch too. A missing token is a configuration error, so it
now raises a StarHistoryAuthRequired subclass that still fails the job. Adds tests.

get_by_id("2401.99999") returned {"title": "Error", ...} instead of raising
"Paper not found". Skip entries whose id is an /api/errors URL. Adds tests.

Scopus answers an empty search with entry: [{"error": "Result set was empty"}].

total 0 plus one phantom result with every field null. Drop entries carrying an
"error" key (ScienceDirect already filtered its equivalent). Adds tests.

item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-downloader): require an open licence before calling an art…
item.description:
fix(nature-downloader): require an open licence before calling an article OA

confirmedOa and the publisher_oa candidate treated any Crossref licence URL as
proof of open access, but paywalled articles routinely carry publisher TDM or
user licences (for example elsevier.com/tdm/userlicense/1.0), so a subscription
article was reported as "confirmed_oa" even when Unpaywall said it was closed.
Only a Creative Commons licence (URL or cc-by style token) now counts. Adds
tests for the TDM case and the CC URL case.

item.title: fix: match a top-level --output path in the star-history README cache…

not rewrite a longer filename such as other-star-history.svg. Adds tests.

item.label: commit

item.title: fix: leave the star-history chart unchanged when stargazer counts dis…

unchanged") when GitHub's reported count and the returned timestamps differ by

now raises a StarHistoryAuthRequired subclass that still fails the job. Adds tests.

item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-downloader): do not overwrite a saved paper that has the s…

with the same title ("Editorial"), or any two direct --pdf-url downloads
without a title, silently destroyed the first and left the manifest sha256 for

different content, and reuse the file when the bytes are identical. Adds tests.

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): keep source-size slides within PowerPoint's 56…

62.5 in wide <p:sldSz> that PowerPoint rejects (its maximum is 56 in per side).

item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): resolve package-absolute OPC relationship targets
item.description:

unchanged, so a relationship Target written as "/ppt/..." (valid OPC) no longer
matched any zip member: the slide read raised KeyError (not caught as the

drops alpha and exposes the colour stored under transparent pixels (normally
black), so a PNG with a transparent background became a black slide

first. Adds tests, including partial alpha and opaque pixels unchanged.

item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): never delete an existing --keep-workdir directory

the page directory) deleted every image in the page's assets folder before
copying the TeX debug files in. Refuse an existing non-empty target that was not
written by this command (marker file), check it before rendering so it cannot
mask a LaTeX error, and still replace its own previous copy. Adds tests.

item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-academic-search): ignore Scopus "Result set was empty" ent…
item.description:

Scopus answers an empty search with entry: [{"error": "Result set was empty"}].
_search_entries passed that dict through, so search("TITLE(xyz)") returned
total 0 plus one phantom result with every field null. Drop entries carrying an
"error" key (ScienceDirect already filtered its equivalent). Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-downloader): require an open licence before calling an art…
item.description:
fix(nature-downloader): require an open licence before calling an article OA

confirmedOa and the publisher_oa candidate treated any Crossref licence URL as
proof of open access, but paywalled articles routinely carry publisher TDM or
user licences (for example elsevier.com/tdm/userlicense/1.0), so a subscription
article was reported as "confirmed_oa" even when Unpaywall said it was closed.
Only a Creative Commons licence (URL or cc-by style token) now counts. Adds
tests for the TDM case and the CC URL case.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-downloader): do not overwrite a saved paper that has the s…
item.description:
fix(nature-downloader): do not overwrite a saved paper that has the same title

saveFullTextResponse named the file from the title (or DOI, or the literal
"article" fallback) and renameSync replaced any existing file, so a second paper
with the same title ("Editorial"), or any two direct --pdf-url downloads
without a title, silently destroyed the first and left the manifest sha256 for
it pointing at the wrong bytes. Add -2, -3, ... when the existing file has
different content, and reuse the file when the bytes are identical. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): keep source-size slides within PowerPoint's 56…
item.description:
fix(nature-image2ppt): keep source-size slides within PowerPoint's 56 in limit

source_size_slide divided pixels by a fixed 96, so a 6000x3000 image produced a
62.5 in wide <p:sldSz> that PowerPoint rejects (its maximum is 56 in per side).
Use a coarser px/inch when either side would exceed 56 in, keeping the aspect
ratio and recording the px_per_inch actually used. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): resolve package-absolute OPC relationship targets
item.description:
fix(nature-image2ppt): resolve package-absolute OPC relationship targets

posixpath.join("ppt", "/ppt/slides/slide1.xml") returns the absolute path
unchanged, so a relationship Target written as "/ppt/..." (valid OPC) no longer
matched any zip member: the slide read raised KeyError (not caught as the
ValueError normalize_inputs expects) and image parts were reported missing even
though they were present. Add join_part() that treats a leading "/" as the
package root and use it for resolve_target and both slide-part joins. Adds
tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): flatten transparent images onto white, not black
item.description:
fix(nature-image2ppt): flatten transparent images onto white, not black

save_image_page and extract_image_based_pptx_pages used convert("RGB"), which
drops alpha and exposes the colour stored under transparent pixels (normally
black), so a PNG with a transparent background became a black slide
background. Composite RGBA/LA/palette-with-transparency images onto white
first. Adds tests, including partial alpha and opaque pixels unchanged.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): never delete an existing --keep-workdir directory
item.description:

the page directory) deleted every image in the page's assets folder before
copying the TeX debug files in. Refuse an existing non-empty target that was not
written by this command (marker file), check it before rendering so it cannot
mask a LaTeX error, and still replace its own previous copy. Adds tests.

item.title: fix(nature-academic-search): make --retry 0 still try once in format-…

efetch_medline, download_crossref and download_arxiv looped over range(retries),

item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-figure): report OpenRouter timeouts and image download fai…
item.description:
fix(nature-figure): report OpenRouter timeouts and image download failures cleanly

request_images only caught HTTPError and URLError, so a socket timeout while
waiting for headers or reading the body escaped as a raw TimeoutError traceback
after the request had already been sent (and billed). The second urlopen that
fetches item["url"] had no handler at all. Catch OSError/TimeoutError for both
and exit with a clear message. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-response): resolve \input of a dotted filename like sec1.f…
item.description:
fix(nature-response): resolve \input of a dotted filename like sec1.final

check_package_consistency appended ".tex" only when the target had no suffix, so
\input{sec1.final} (a file named sec1.final.tex) looked for "sec1.final", failed
is_file(), and the include was left unexpanded; the checker then silently skipped
that section's text. Follow LaTeX: try name.tex first, then the literal name.
Adds tests, including explicit .tex and extensionless existing files.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix: match a top-level --output path in the star-history README cache…
item.description:
fix: match a top-level --output path in the star-history README cache-buster

For `--output star-history.svg` PurePosixPath(...).parent is ".", so the pattern
required a literal "./" prefix and matched nothing: the SVG was written, then
update_readme_cache_buster raised RuntimeError and left the README stale.
Omit the directory prefix for a top-level file and anchor the match so it does
not rewrite a longer filename such as other-star-history.svg. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix: leave the star-history chart unchanged when stargazer counts dis…
item.description:
fix: leave the star-history chart unchanged when stargazer counts disagree

fetch_stargazers raised StarHistoryUnavailable ("leaving the existing chart
unchanged") when GitHub's reported count and the returned timestamps differ by
more than 100, but main only caught that exception around build_daily_points, so
the job crashed with a traceback and exit 1 instead of warning and returning 0.
Catch it around the fetch too. A missing token is a configuration error, so it
now raises a StarHistoryAuthRequired subclass that still fails the job. Adds tests.

posixpath.join("ppt", "/ppt/slides/slide1.xml") returns the absolute path
unchanged, so a relationship Target written as "/ppt/..." (valid OPC) no longer
matched any zip member: the slide read raised KeyError (not caught as the
ValueError normalize_inputs expects) and image parts were reported missing even
though they were present. Add join_part() that treats a leading "/" as the
package root and use it for resolve_target and both slide-part joins. Adds
tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): flatten transparent images onto white, not black
item.description:
fix(nature-image2ppt): flatten transparent images onto white, not black

save_image_page and extract_image_based_pptx_pages used convert("RGB"), which
drops alpha and exposes the colour stored under transparent pixels (normally
black), so a PNG with a transparent background became a black slide
background. Composite RGBA/LA/palette-with-transparency images onto white
first. Adds tests, including partial alpha and opaque pixels unchanged.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): never delete an existing --keep-workdir directory
item.description:
fix(nature-image2ppt): never delete an existing --keep-workdir directory

_maybe_keep_workdir called shutil.rmtree on the target whenever it existed, so
`formula render-latex --keep-workdir assets` (accepted because assets/ is inside
the page directory) deleted every image in the page's assets folder before
copying the TeX debug files in. Refuse an existing non-empty target that was not
written by this command (marker file), check it before rendering so it cannot
mask a LaTeX error, and still replace its own previous copy. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix: ignore code-fenced "##" lines in update-reference-tocs.py
item.description:
fix: ignore code-fenced "##" lines in update-reference-tocs.py

The heading scan matched any "## " line, including shell comments inside fenced
code blocks, so a long reference containing such a block got a bogus Contents
entry. Track fence state and skip headings inside it. Adds a test.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix: match GitHub heading anchors in update-reference-tocs.py
item.description:
fix: match GitHub heading anchors in update-reference-tocs.py

github_anchor collapsed runs of spaces and hyphens, but GitHub turns each
space into a hyphen without collapsing, so "Input - Output" is
"input---output" and "A & B" is "a--b". Generated Contents links for such
headings pointed at nonexistent anchors. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-academic-search): make --retry 0 still try once in format-…
item.description:
fix(nature-academic-search): make --retry 0 still try once in format-converter

efetch_medline, download_crossref and download_arxiv looped over range(retries),
so --retry 0 skipped the loop entirely: download_crossref then hit
UnboundLocalError on `data`, and the other two returned nothing. Use
max(1, retries) attempts. Adds tests for a successful and a failing download.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-figure): report OpenRouter timeouts and image download fai…
item.description:
fix(nature-figure): report OpenRouter timeouts and image download failures cleanly

request_images only caught HTTPError and URLError, so a socket timeout while
waiting for headers or reading the body escaped as a raw TimeoutError traceback
after the request had already been sent (and billed). The second urlopen that
fetches item["url"] had no handler at all. Catch OSError/TimeoutError for both
and exit with a clear message. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-response): resolve \input of a dotted filename like sec1.f…
item.description:
fix(nature-response): resolve \input of a dotted filename like sec1.final

check_package_consistency appended ".tex" only when the target had no suffix, so
\input{sec1.final} (a file named sec1.final.tex) looked for "sec1.final", failed
is_file(), and the include was left unexpanded; the checker then silently skipped
that section's text. Follow LaTeX: try name.tex first, then the literal name.
Adds tests, including explicit .tex and extensionless existing files.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix: match a top-level --output path in the star-history README cache…
item.description:
fix: match a top-level --output path in the star-history README cache-buster

For `--output star-history.svg` PurePosixPath(...).parent is ".", so the pattern
required a literal "./" prefix and matched nothing: the SVG was written, then
update_readme_cache_buster raised RuntimeError and left the README stale.
Omit the directory prefix for a top-level file and anchor the match so it does
not rewrite a longer filename such as other-star-history.svg. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix: leave the star-history chart unchanged when stargazer counts dis…
item.description:
fix: leave the star-history chart unchanged when stargazer counts disagree

fetch_stargazers raised StarHistoryUnavailable ("leaving the existing chart
unchanged") when GitHub's reported count and the returned timestamps differ by
more than 100, but main only caught that exception around build_daily_points, so
the job crashed with a traceback and exit 1 instead of warning and returning 0.
Catch it around the fetch too. A missing token is a configuration error, so it
now raises a StarHistoryAuthRequired subclass that still fails the job. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-academic-search): skip arXiv error entries instead of retu…
item.description:
fix(nature-academic-search): skip arXiv error entries instead of returning a paper

arXiv reports a bad request as an <entry> with id http://arxiv.org/api/errors#...
and title "Error". The id regex matched the trailing NNNN.NNNNN, so
get_by_id("2401.99999") returned {"title": "Error", ...} instead of raising
"Paper not found". Skip entries whose id is an /api/errors URL. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-academic-search): ignore Scopus "Result set was empty" ent…
item.description:
fix(nature-academic-search): ignore Scopus "Result set was empty" entries

Scopus answers an empty search with entry: [{"error": "Result set was empty"}].
_search_entries passed that dict through, so search("TITLE(xyz)") returned
total 0 plus one phantom result with every field null. Drop entries carrying an
"error" key (ScienceDirect already filtered its equivalent). Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-downloader): require an open licence before calling an art…
item.description:
fix(nature-downloader): require an open licence before calling an article OA

confirmedOa and the publisher_oa candidate treated any Crossref licence URL as
proof of open access, but paywalled articles routinely carry publisher TDM or
user licences (for example elsevier.com/tdm/userlicense/1.0), so a subscription
article was reported as "confirmed_oa" even when Unpaywall said it was closed.
Only a Creative Commons licence (URL or cc-by style token) now counts. Adds
tests for the TDM case and the CC URL case.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-downloader): do not overwrite a saved paper that has the s…
item.description:
fix(nature-downloader): do not overwrite a saved paper that has the same title

saveFullTextResponse named the file from the title (or DOI, or the literal
"article" fallback) and renameSync replaced any existing file, so a second paper
with the same title ("Editorial"), or any two direct --pdf-url downloads
without a title, silently destroyed the first and left the manifest sha256 for
it pointing at the wrong bytes. Add -2, -3, ... when the existing file has
different content, and reuse the file when the bytes are identical. Adds tests.

Xinrui Ma
item.label: commit

item.title: fix(nature-image2ppt): keep source-size slides within PowerPoint's 56…
item.description:
fix(nature-image2ppt): keep source-size slides within PowerPoint's 56 in limit

source_size_slide divided pixels by a fixed 96, so a 6000x3000 image produced a
62.5 in wide <p:sldSz> that PowerPoint rejects (its maximum is 56 in per side).
Use a coarser px/inch when either side would exceed 56 in, keeping the aspect
ratio and recording the px_per_inch actually used. Adds tests.

item.title: feat(nature-paper-xray): 新增单篇论文精读技能
item.description:
feat(nature-paper-xray): 新增单篇论文精读技能

新增 `nature-paper-xray`：把一篇给定论文读到能复述作者的推理，而不是复述摘要。

它做四件事：

- 还原作者真实的出发点——这一步要解决前人的哪个具体问题；论文没讲就写论文没讲，不替作者编动机
- 分清承重与装饰——这个设计拿掉会塌，还是顺手加的；有消融或附录能判断就指出来，没有就写论文没做这个对照
- 公式落到能手算的例子——每个符号给形状和含义，关键公式后面跟一个微型例子，写具体数字算到底
- 核对证据边界——正文数字与图表是否一致、基线对照条件是否对齐、超参是否只在测试集上挑、有没有预处理泄漏、代价与结论失效的条件

划界：只读不判。它报告论文做了什么、证据够到哪儿，不评分、不排名、不判录用成熟度或新颖性
（那是 nature-reviewer）；不提炼写作范式、不翻译、不检索文献、不核验引用、不代写正文。

文件：

- `SKILL.md`——立场、工作流、按论文类型调整阅读重心、边界、输出规范
- `references/deep-reading-protocol.md`——精读顺序、能手算例子的标准、承重判定、交付物结构与失败模式
- `references/evidence-boundary.md`——数字一致性、基线对齐、选择压力、泄漏、代价与范围、缺口如何如实写、严重度分级
- `README.md` / `README_EN.md`——中英镜像，六个基础章节
- `manifest.yaml`、`agents/openai.yaml`

同时更新根 README 的技能索引（中英各加一行）与技能数徽章 20 → 21。

本地校验：

  python scripts/validate-readme-mirror.py    passed, 22 mirrored skill docs checked
  python scripts/validate-skill-index.py      passed, 21 triggerable skills, 22 listed entries
  python scripts/validate-readmes.py          passed
  python scripts/validate-repository.py       passed, 22 skill directories checked
  python -m pytest -q scripts/tests           12

feat(nature-paper-xray): 新增单篇论文精读技能

新增 `nature-paper-xray`：把一篇给定论文读到能复述作者的推理，而不是复述摘要。

它做四件事：

- 还原作者真实的出发点——这一步要解决前人的哪个具体问题；论文没讲就写论文没讲，不替作者编动机
- 分清承重与装饰——这个设计拿掉会塌，还是顺手加的；有消融或附录能判断就指出来，没有就写论文没做这个对照
- 公式落到能手算的例子——每个符号给形状和含义，关键公式后面跟一个微型例子，写具体数字算到底
- 核对证据边界——正文数字与图表是否一致、基线对照条件是否对齐、超参是否只在测试集上挑、有没有预处理泄漏、代价与结论失效的条件

划界：只读不判。它报告论文做了什么、证据够到哪儿，不评分、不排名、不判录用成熟度或新颖性
（那是 nature-reviewer）；不提炼写作范式、不翻译、不检索文献、不核验引用、不代写正文。
